name: HP 438A dual-channel power meter
description: Two-channel thermocouple/diode power meter for the HP 8480-series sensors: readings in W or dBm, A, B, ratio and difference modes, per-channel cal factor, offset, range and filter, REL, ZERO and CAL ADJ against the 1 mW / 50 MHz POWER REF, which is the meter's one output.

quirks.note: Pre-IEEE 488.2 HP-IB program codes. No *IDN? (it answers ?ID, p. 3-40), no *OPC?, no error queue. The manifest's identify and keepalive (a serial poll) tell the core.
The reading is sent whenever the meter is addressed to talk in free run (p. 3-34); it is not a query reply. The driver reads it with nothing sent first.
9.0000E+40 is what the meter sends while its display shows an error (p. 3-35). It becomes reading = null, and the Status Message's error code says why.

ZERO and CAL ADJ take seconds and any command aborts them (p. 3-49). While one runs, the driver only serial-polls for status bit 1 (Cal/Zero Complete, p. 3-45) and refuses every action. ALL OUTPUTS OFF still goes through, and aborts it.
PR and a Device Clear are the same (p. 3-70): both cal factors go to 100% and both offsets to 0 dB (p. 3-69), so the next readings are silently off by the sensor's cal factor. Neither is ever sent.
RC is not offered: a stored setup includes the POWER REF state (p. 3-84), so recalling one can switch the output on.

In trigger hold (TR0) the meter outputs nothing but its serial-poll byte (p. 3-33), so it cannot even answer ?ID and looks switched off. The driver never leaves free run; if another program left it in hold, cycle its LINE switch (free run is the turn-on default, p. 3-30).
CAL ADJ calibrates one channel with the sensor on it; both channels must be calibrated with their own sensors (p. 3-48). Zero first (p. 3-49).
A channel with no sensor shows error 31 (A) or 32 (B) (p. 3-58). At power-up that is the documented pass condition, not a fault.
In ratio and REL modes the bus value is % or dB (p. 3-53). How a linear % is scaled on the bus (100 or 1.00 for equal power) is not stated in the manual and has not been seen on this bench yet.

author: Systemstech

manual.title: HP 438A Power Meter Operating and Service Manual
manual.pages: ref = page printed on the page (section 3: printed 3-N = PDF page N + 30). Program codes: Table 3-7, p. 3-47.

measure.doc: Measurement mode: one sensor, a ratio or a difference. Changing it clears the filter and drops REL.

value.doc: A, B, A/B, B/A, A-B or B-A

measure.scpi: AP | BP | AR | BR | AD | BD

units.doc: Readings in watts (linear) or dBm (log). Ratio and REL readings become % or dB.

cal_factor.doc: The sensor's CAL FACTOR at the measurement frequency, from its label. Selects the channel for entry (SET A / SET B).

offset.doc: dB added to the sensor's power: positive for gain ahead of it, negative for loss.

range.doc: Power range for one channel: auto, hold (keep the current auto range), or manual 1 (most sensitive) to 5.

filter.doc: Averaging for one channel: auto, hold, or manual 0-9 (the average of 2^n readings).

rel.doc: REL on: the next reading becomes the reference and later ones are shown relative to it, in dB or %. The reference cannot be read back.

osc.doc: The POWER REF output, 1.00 mW at 50 MHz. ON needs confirmed=True, and a script run must be allowed outputs.

zero.doc: Zero one channel. No RF may be on its sensor: any applied power becomes an offset in every later reading. Takes about 10 s; nothing else is sent until it finishes.

cal_adj.doc: CAL ADJ: calibrate one channel's gain to its sensor on the 1 mW POWER REF (the meter switches the reference on itself). ref_cf is the sensor's REFERENCE cal factor at 50 MHz, from its label. Zero the channel first.

reading.doc: the reading, in `unit`; null while the meter shows an error (it sends 9.0000E+40)

unit.doc: what `reading` is in: W, dBm, % or dB (p. 3-53)

meas_error.doc: measurement error code from the Status Message, Table 3-8 (null = none)

mode.doc: A, B, A/B, B/A, A-B, B-A, or zeroing / cal while one runs

entry_channel.doc: the channel settings go to (SET A / SET B)

trigger.doc: free run (always, from this plugin) or hold

range.doc: range 1 (most sensitive) to 5, 10 dB each (p. 3-71); null before the first auto-range

filter.doc: filter number 0-9: the reading averages 2^n samples (p. 3-60)

cal_factor.doc: CAL FACTOR in use for this sensor, from the learn string

offset.doc: OFFSET added to this sensor's power, from the learn string

range.doc: range 1 (most sensitive) to 5, 10 dB each (p. 3-71); null before the first auto-range

filter.doc: filter number 0-9: the reading averages 2^n samples (p. 3-60)

cal_factor.doc: CAL FACTOR in use for this sensor, from the learn string

offset.doc: OFFSET added to this sensor's power, from the learn string

busy.doc: the ZERO or CAL ADJ running now, with seconds so far; null when idle

last_op.doc: how the last ZERO or CAL ADJ ended

status_raw.doc: the 23-character Status Message as received (Figure 3-6, p. 3-40)
